messages:
talia: Noting an ongoing issue: since ~12:07 UTC some hosted and dedicated customers in us-central are seeing elevated tail latency and sporadic 502s. early telemetry points to a KV-cache admission controller regression. opening incident thread and triage. https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1865140021
ben: oncall here. observed kv-admission queue growing after the new per-tenant token bucket hit bursts; it appears the controller is favoring small reads and starving large prefix reads, which causes head-of-line blocking. put a soft throttle on low-priority embed reads and enabled prioritization overrides for committed dedicated lanes. immediate error rate down from ~4.8% -> ~1.1%.
kai: root cause investigation: the admission-controller rewrite from last week added a heuristic that biases by recent hit-rate; under bursty traffic that causes oscillation and reenqueue storms. preparing a revert patch to restore deterministic fairness and a fallback limiter. planning a canary rollout to us-central.
infra: deploy-bot: starting canary rollback of kv-admission v0.9.1 -> v0.8.6 in us-central, batch 1/3. sha=cc3d2a. CI: https://ci.redwood/build/8331
ops-bot: monitor: kv-admission-throttle alert fired id=kv-adm-4512. queue depth trending down following throttle and override changes.
ben: mitigation checklist: 1) soft throttle non-critical embed reads (done), 2) prioritize committed dedicated lanes (done), 3) canary rollback in us-central (in progress), 4) enable hosted-fallback routes for highest-priority customers (done), 5) customer outreach (in progress). status doc: https://go.redwood/incident/1865140021
support: sent an interim customer message to affected accounts: "We're investigating increased latency and intermittent 502s in us-central tied to cache admission behavior. We've applied prioritization and are rolling a rollback. We'll follow up when we have a full resolution."
kai: canary batch 1 looks good; p95 back to baseline on canary shards. scheduling batch 2 now with close monitoring. adding a short-term circuit-breaker to limit reenqueue depth while we roll.
infra: deploy-bot: canary batch 2 complete, batch 3 queued. new circuit-breaker config rolled: reenqueue_limit=8, backoff_ms=250-2000.
ben: after batch 3 rollout, overall tail latency normalized and 502s dropped to ~0.1%. keeping the circuit-breaker and fairness revert in place for 2 hours before relaxing.
talia: setting incident severity=SEV2 for tracking and exec note. postmortem owners: kai (RCA) and ben (mitigations & follow-ups). follow-ups: add admission-controller unit+load tests for oscillation, improve canary traffic mix, and document reenqueue limits. final incident doc will include timeline and customer outreach log. quick link to incident updates: https://go.redwood/incident/1865140021/updates
